chapter: Porch interview and Jazz Train plans
title: Not a performer but with his own stamp
summary: He says he was never a performer, and Rasch says his playing is his own.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: (Inaudible) because you got jobs in the normal way, just like anyone else. Just the way they do today. (Inaudible).
Did you perform as well as (inaudible)?

No, not me. I was never a performer. That's right, I never (inaudible). I would never classify myself as a pianist, because the pianists that I've heard are good, they're so superior. They could play with their eyes closed that you've never played if you studied for 100 years.
But you have a -- your own stamp. You

play things that I've never heard anyone else do with the piano. You've got a idea that's just not noodling. You have your own genius. It's very hard sometimes for -- when things come easy to somebody, for them to realize that that's exceptional.
Yes, that's right, because you've got to put your own individuality into what you're doing. And (inaudible) that you put into it. It's as simple as that.
